paper.title: Fast Rates for Bandit PAC Multiclass Classification

settings.name_in_paper: Agnostic PAC bandit multiclass classification (finite hypothesis class)
unmapped: multiclass classification structure: each example has a single correct label, reward is 1{predicted label = true label}
goal is to output a hypothesis eps-optimal w.r.t. expected zero-one loss relative to the best hypothesis in finite class H (N = |H|)
settings.definition_quote: The environment generates a pair $(x_i, y_i) \sim \calD$ and the example $x_i$ is revealed to the learner; The learner predicts a label $\wh{y}_i \in \calY$; The learner observes whether or not the classification of $x_i$ is correct, namely $\ind{\wh{y}_i = y_i}$. ... the goal of the learner is to produce a hypothesis $\hat{h}$ such that with probability at least $1 - \delta$: $L_\calD(\hat{h}) - L_\calD(h^\star) \leq \eps$

settings.name_in_paper: Agnostic PAC bandit multiclass classification (Natarajan class)
unmapped: multiclass classification structure: single correct label per example, reward 1{prediction correct}
possibly infinite hypothesis class with finite Natarajan dimension d_N
settings.definition_quote: Let $\calH : \calX \to \calY$ be a hypothesis class of finite Natarajan dimension $d_N$.

algorithms.name: Bandit PAC Multiclass Classification via Log Barrier Stochastic Optimization (Algorithm 1, with SPIDER Frank-Wolfe)

tuning: Frank-Wolfe run for T = Theta((K^4/gamma^4) sqrt(log(N/delta))) rounds, eta_t = 1/t, batch sizes b_t = (gamma/2K)^2 t^2 for t = 2^k - 1 and b_t = t otherwise

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: If we set $\gamma = \frac12$, $M_1 = \Theta(K^8 \log \brk{N / \delta})$, $M_2 = \Theta \brk*{\log \brk{N / \delta} \brk*{K / \eps + 1 / \eps^2}}$ and use \cref{alg:fw-main} ... then with probability at least $1-\delta$ \cref{alg:bandit-pac} outputs $\hat{h} \in \calH$ with $L_\calD(\hat{h}) - L_\calD(h^\star) \leq \eps$, using a total sample complexity of $O ((K^9 + \frac{1}{\eps^2}) \log\frac{N}{\delta})$. Furthermore, ... makes a total number of $O(K^4 \sqrt{\log(N / \delta)})$ calls to the weighted ERM oracle ..., and runs in total time polynomial in $K$, $1/\eps$ and $\log(N/\delta)$.

results.notes: N = |H| mapped to N_exp. Polynomial time given a weighted ERM oracle over H (O(K^4 sqrt(log(N/delta))) oracle calls). Proper learner.

symbols.d_N: Natarajan dimension of the hypothesis class H

conditions: H has finite Natarajan dimension d_N

source.label: thm:natarajan-main
source.quote: Let $\calH : \calX \to \calY$ be a hypothesis class of finite Natarajan dimension $d_N$. Then there exists a bandit multiclass classification algorithm which outputs a hypothesis $\hat h$ with $L_\calD(\hat h) - \inf_{h \in \calH} L_\calD(h) \leq \eps$ with a sample complexity of $\smash{\widetilde{O}} \brk{\brk{K^9 + \ifrac{1}{\eps^2}}d_N \log(\ifrac{1}{\delta})}$.

results.notes: Obtained via Proposition 1 (cover of size S built from s unlabeled samples) plus Theorem 1; success with probability 1-delta implied by the PAC setup. Learner is improper/cover-based; compute not discussed.
